title: Harmonize grid & interaction patterns for dashboards, rollouts, and cost views
creator: Ava Mendoza
description: Goal: Create a unified set of responsive layout rules and interaction patterns for Redwood Console pages (dashboards, rollout pages, and cost views) that behave consistently across modern Chromium, Firefox, and Safari on desktop and mobile. Deliverables include a Figma prototype, a small CSS utility bundle (grid + density tokens), documented fallbacks for problematic browser behaviors, and a review-ready spec to hand to frontend engineering. Focus areas: table density & virtualization, chart rendering strategy (SVG vs canvas), modal stacking and focus traps, tooltip/overflow behavior, sticky headers, and responsive card/grid behavior for dashboard panels.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff with PM and Eng — outlined scope and prioritized pages: billing cost-explorer, model rollouts list, customer dashboard overview.
2026-03-11: Exploratory prototype in Figma (desktop and three mobile breakpoints). Experimented with 4 density modes and two grid systems (12-col CSS Grid vs hybrid flex + CSS Grid).

2026-03-12: Discovered Safari stacking/position:sticky issues when parent uses transform; added workaround pattern that avoids transforms on scroll containers and uses top:0 sticky fallback for sticky headers.
2026-03-12: Built interactive prototype for modal stacking (canary can open nested toggles) and verified focus trap and ESC handling flows. Documented keyboard flows and aria roles.
2026-03-13: Internal design review with PM/Eng. Collected engineering feasibility notes (virtualization and canvas scaling). Updated spec to reflect perf constraints and cross-browser fallbacks.
decisions: Use a primary CSS Grid 12-column layout for wide viewports, fallback to a single-column stacking flow under 720px. Grid gutters use design tokens: --space-2 for compact, --space-4 default.
Adopt a density token system (compact / comfortable / spacious) to let product teams toggle row heights. Compact is default for cost views with large row counts.

Charts: prefer SVG for small multi-series charts and interactive overlays. Use canvas for large-timeseries and heatmaps with pixel-density scaling (devicePixelRatio) and a lightweight interaction layer built on top for hover/tooltips.

Modal behavior: single top-layer modal allowed. For nested dialogs, adopt a non-blocking drawer pattern instead to avoid complex stacking across browsers. Always trap focus and restore focus to opener on close.
Tooltips and overflow hints should prefer portal mounting at document root to avoid clipping; implement a minimal collision detection using boundingClientRect with fallback anchor repositioning.
Sticky table headers: implement sticky + transform-free scroll containers. Where sticky is unreliable (older Safari), fall back to cloning header row and toggling fixed positioning via JS.
Avoid transform on scrollable parents and avoid -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch on containers with sticky elements when possible; document exceptions for mobile momentum scroll needs.
tradeoffs: SVG provides crisp vector scaled interactions but has performance limits for very large point sets; canvas improves frame rates at the cost of accessible native interactions — we mitigate by layering an SVG or HTML interaction surface over the canvas.
Using cloned headers for Safari fallback adds implementation complexity and small paint cost, but ensures column alignment in constrained browsers vs relying on CSS sticky alone.
Drawer fallback for nested modal flows improves cross-browser robustness but deviates from classic nested-modal semantics; this is acceptable for the small number of deep dialogs in Console.
Density tokens add an extra layer of customization and QA, but provide large cost-savings UX wins for power users looking to scan tables quickly.
review_feedback: PM (Katherine O'Neill): Prefer denser default for cost table; request a toggle in the header for switching density per-user.
Frontend lead (Diego Alvarez): Concerned about canvas hover precision on Safari Mobile — recommend an early tech spike to validate devicePixelRatio scaling and pointer event mapping.
Eng QA (Maya Patel): Request explicit test cases for column alignment when using virtualization and sticky headers under heavy scroll loads.
Design Ops (Noah Brooks): Add tokenized spacing examples and a migration plan for existing dashboard panels that use legacy paddings.
acceptance_criteria: All three target pages render without horizontal overflow at breakpoints: 320px, 480px, 720px, 1024px, 1440px.
Modal flows pass keyboard navigation tests: tab order respects focus trap, ESC closes, focus returns to opener.
Charts degrade gracefully: SVG charts and small canvases render correctly in Chromium, Firefox, and Safari on macOS and iOS; interactions show tooltips and highlight on hover/tap.
Sticky headers remain visible and aligned across supported browsers; Safari fallback (cloned header) enabled only when native sticky fails.
Cost-explorer table supports virtualization with correct row height across density modes and passes column-resize tests and selection interactions.
No regressions in a11y scans (axe-core) — color contrast and focus indicators meet current accessibility tokens.
testing_plan: Run cross-browser visual diff snapshots for desktop breakpoints using BrowserStack + Percy.
Manual QA checklist for keyboard flows and focus management across all pages.
Perf budget: interactive time-to-first-response for chart interactions < 120ms on p95 for hosted-demo machine.
Edge-case tests: large table with 50k rows virtualized, charts with 10k points, modal nested open/close cycles.
Regression doc: list pre-existing components that will be touched and require smoke tests (Table, Modal, Tooltip, Chart wrapper).
notes_for_engineering: Spike tasks: ENG-2520 (canvas hi-dpi spike), ENG-2489 (virtualized sticky header refactor).
Provide small CSS utility module with tokens and a demo page for engineers to integrate and test in isolation.
Avoid global transforms on containers that host sticky elements; prefer compositing hints (will-change: transform) only where necessary and tested.
Add e2e tests that run headless Safari (via Playwright) to catch sticky/clipping regressions early.
